name: halftone-reveal
title: Halftone Reveal
description: A photograph printed as a coarse two-colour halftone. Where the pointer moves the dots swell open and the sharp picture shows through, and a click spreads a clearing ring across the print.
use: A hero or gallery image that should look printed until the visitor explores it with the pointer.
avoid: Reveal needs a mouse, so touch users only see the halftone, and the red ink fights other palettes.
a11y: The photo is drawn to a canvas with no alt text or role, and the reveal answers only to a pointer. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A smiling woman with dark hair and a red top fills the frame, rendered as large halftone dots in brick red against pale cream. Under the cursor a soft round patch turns smooth and photographic, showing her face and hair clearly.
behaves: The whole picture stays as a dotted print while a soft-edged brush follows the pointer and converts the dots to the real photograph inside its reach. The revealed patch lingers briefly then fades back, and clicking sends a widening clear ring outward.
customise: Set src plus fit, mode, dot shape, cell size, angle and the ink and paper colours. Reveal radius, softness, linger, reverse, wander and click burst are props.
weight: heavy: A full-screen halftone shader plus a brush mask pass run every frame while the pointer moves.
demo: A portrait of a smiling woman with dark hair and a red top against a warm outdoor background.
issues: The top of the head is cropped off in every frame, so the portrait feels accidentally cut.
The dots are very large, so facial detail disappears outside the reveal.
polishWhy: Convincing print texture and a satisfying reveal; the crop cuts the head and the dots are coarse.
